Sets the pipe resonance together with the speed of sound: the quarter-wave sits at c / 4L and the odd harmonics above it land among the firing orders, which is what gives the exhaust a pitch of its own independent of engine speed. Longer is deeper. Both duct delay buffers are sized from this at construction.

Cross-section of the duct. The aftertreatment box is a compliance, and a compliance behaves like an added duct length of volume over area, so without an area the box cannot say what it does to the pipe. Larger area means the same box lengthens the duct less.

Reflection coefficient at the pipe mouth. Negative because an open end is a pressure node and inverts the wave. Its magnitude is how much of each pulse is returned to form a standing wave rather than radiated away: nearer zero is a duct with no note, nearer one is a duct that rings too long and too evenly. It is also half the waveguide's loop gain, so validation requires it to stay inside (-1, 0) or the duct is unstable.

One-pole loss on the reflected wave, standing for the fact that a pipe mouth radiates poorly at low frequency and well high up. It is why a real pipe's low resonances are sharp and its high ones are damped. Lower values damp the pipe more and make the note duller and shorter.

The box is a compliance shunted on the duct, which at the wavelengths that set the first few resonances behaves like an extra length of volume over area. So it lowers the pipe's resonance rather than filtering it. The approximation is a low-frequency one and stops describing the box once a wavelength is comparable with the box's own dimensions; nothing in the audible exhaust note is up there.
invented test value for `exhaust_system.aftertreatment_transmission`

Broadband attenuation across the turbine, applied above the corner below. Acoustically a turbine is a large silencer, and this is the term that makes the engine read as turbocharged rather than as open-piped. Too little and the exhaust is raw and sharp; too much and the exhaust note disappears behind the block noise.
Corner above which the turbine's insertion loss applies. Below it the pulse passes; above it the loss is taken. Moving it down mutes more of the pulse's edge and leaves more of its fundamental.

Shortest exhaust manifold runner. With the longest it sets the spread of arrival times at the turbine, which is what makes an inline six sound like an inline six rather than like six identical pops - and what makes geometry.firing_order audible at all rather than merely validated.

Longest exhaust manifold runner. Given as a span with the minimum rather than a length per cylinder, so this section carries no cylinder count and a configuration with a different number of cylinders uses it unchanged. Validation requires it to exceed the minimum: a manifold whose runners are all one length cannot make the firing order audible.

Breaks the cylinder-to-cylinder symmetry of the exhaust pulse train. Six bit-identical cylinders sum to a mathematically pure harmonic comb with no jitter and no amplitude scatter, and the ear hears that as synthesised rather than as an engine. Drawn once per cylinder at reset from the reset seed, never per step, so determinism is exact. Deliberately far too small to move any calibration result: a spread that shifts peak power is not modelling a tolerance, and the validator caps it at 0.1 for that reason.

Sets the level of the structural radiation path against the exhaust path. The structural path is combustion noise: the premixed pressure rise ringing the block, head and covers, which is what makes a diesel identifiable as one rather than as a generic engine. Too low and the engine is a low-frequency drone; too high and the clatter both swamps the exhaust note and drives the sum into the soft-clip knee, where saturation invents harmonics in the band being measured and the improvement becomes an artefact of clipping rather than of the model.

provenance.value_note: invented test values for `audio.structural_modes`: three modes at 1100, 2000 and 3200 Hz weighted 1.0, 4.0 and 8.0. Three rather than four, and higher, because a smaller block rings higher. Different from the OM 471 bank on purpose, so this fixture proves the modal path is driven by configuration rather than by anything engine-specific in the solver.
provenance.purpose: The modal bank the cylinder-pressure rise rings. Each mode is one two-pole resonator standing for a bending or breathing mode of the engine's outer surface, which radiates straight to air rather than down the exhaust. The frequencies set where the clatter sits and the Q values set how long it rings; an iron structure rings for a few milliseconds, which is Q in the tens. Pole radius 1 - pi f dt / Q must stay inside (0, 1) or the mode is unstable, and validation rejects that rather than letting it grow in the hot loop.

Detunes the boost loop against the brake's positive feedback.

Gives each cycle its own delivered fuel quantity, so no two firing events are identical even from the same cylinder. The per-cylinder sibling gives each cylinder a fixed character; this is the other defect, and a different one. With build scatter alone every cycle of a given cylinder is bit-identical to its last and the output is a comb of infinitely narrow lines, which the ear hears as a synthesiser rather than as an engine. Real diesels run a few percent cycle-to-cycle variation in indicated work from injector shot-to-shot spread, residual mixing and turbulence, and that is what gives the firing orders their width. Drawn once per cylinder per cycle at intake valve closing from the reset seed, never per step, so determinism and batch invariance are untouched. The smoke limit still applies after the trim.

Sets the level of the torque-driven body path against the exhaust path. This is the path that carries the roar: the engine reacting against its mounts, shaking the frame and cab panels between roughly 20 and 200 Hz. It is not a variation on the structural path and cannot be replaced by one, because it is driven by a different quantity - crank torque swings through the whole cycle at the firing frequency and its low orders, while cylinder pressure spikes once per cycle with a fast premixed edge and drives the hundreds-of-hertz modes. Too low and a 12.8 litre six sounds like a much smaller engine; too high and the output is dominated by content below 80 Hz, which is headroom spent where no ordinary speaker reproduces anything.

The modal bank the fluctuating crank torque shakes through the engine mounts. Each mode is one two-pole resonator standing for a frame or cab panel resonance. The Q values are deliberately far lower than the structural bank's: a panel on a trimmed cab is heavily damped, and a sharp bank here would be a tonal drone that jumped in level as the firing frequency swept past each mode rather than a roar that tracks engine speed smoothly. Pole radius 1 - pi f dt / Q must stay inside (0, 1) or the mode is unstable, and validation rejects that rather than letting it grow in the hot loop.
